options.why: Confuses the slope with the elasticity; elasticity also depends on the price-quantity ratio.

payload.stem: A firm in perfectly competitive output and labor markets pays a wage of $26. The marginal revenue product of its last worker is $30. To maximize profit, what should the firm do?

options.text: Shut down, because the wage and MRP differ.
options.why: Confuses a hiring adjustment with a shutdown decision.

options.text: Keep employment unchanged, because both the wage and the marginal revenue product are positive.
options.why: Positive values do not imply that profit is maximized; MRP must equal the wage.

options.text: Hire fewer workers, because total revenue exceeds total cost.
options.why: Compares totals instead of the marginal hiring rule.

options.text: Hire more workers, because the marginal revenue product of the next worker exceeds the wage.
options.why: A competitive firm hires labor until MRP equals the wage; here MRP is $30 and the wage is $26, so it should adjust employment accordingly.

options.text: Hire more workers, because the average product of labor is above the wage.
options.why: Compares average product, not marginal revenue product, with the wage.

payload.stem: The owner of a tutoring business earns annual revenue of $300,000, pays explicit costs of $120,000, and gives up $30,000 per year that the owner could earn by working elsewhere. What is the economic profit?

options.why: Reports total revenue without subtracting any costs. The amount is therefore a different quantity from the profit measure the question asks for, so it does not answer the question.
Adds the implicit costs to revenue instead of subtracting them. The amount is therefore a different quantity from the profit measure the question asks for, so it does not answer the question.

Economic profit is revenue minus both the explicit and the implicit costs, so it is lower than accounting profit by the value of the opportunities the owner gives up, which makes it the measure that includes every opportunity cost.
Subtracts only the implicit costs from revenue. The amount is therefore a different quantity from the profit measure the question asks for, so it does not answer the question.
Reports accounting profit instead of economic profit. The amount is therefore a different quantity from the profit measure the question asks for, so it does not answer the question.

payload.stem: Which of the following statements about economic choices is correct?

options.text: Scarcity affects only the production of goods and not the use of time.
options.why: Limits scarcity to goods; time is also a limited resource that must be allocated.

options.text: Efficient resource allocation eliminates scarcity.
options.why: Confuses efficiency with abundance; efficient allocation still leaves wants unsatisfied.

options.text: Because resources are scarce, producing more of one good requires producing less of another.
options.why: With scarce resources, using more of them for one good leaves fewer for others, so a trade-off exists.

options.text: A good that is free to consumers has no opportunity cost to society.
options.why: Treats a zero price as a zero cost; resources used to make the good have alternative uses.

options.text: A wealthy society can produce unlimited quantities of every good and does not face trade-offs.
options.why: Believes wealth removes scarcity; even rich societies have limited resources and face trade-offs.
